value.overview: The Crested Bobwhite (Colinus cristatus) is a small, ground-dwelling quail of open and lightly wooded habitats. It has a distinctive forward-pointing crest, patterned brown, buff, black, and rufous plumage, and a compact body adapted for walking through dense grass. Unlike many migratory birds, it remains in suitable areas year-round. In Costa Rica, it is a localized resident at the southwestern edge of its range, especially in lowlands near the Golfo Dulce region and the Panamanian border.
value.classification: The Crested Bobwhite belongs to the quail family Odontophoridae and the order Galliformes. It is closely related to other New World quail, including the Spot-bellied Bobwhite, which occurs farther north in Central America.
value.identification: This quail is about 20 cm long and has a short, rounded body with a prominent crest of elongated pale or dark-tipped feathers on the forehead and crown. The upperparts are dark brown and finely patterned, while the face and throat show rufous, gray, black, and white markings. The underparts are heavily spotted and barred with black and warm rufous. Males often show stronger white spotting on the breast; females are generally duller and more buff-colored.
value.rangeHabitat: The Crested Bobwhite occurs from southwestern Costa Rica through western Panama and across much of northern and central South America, with additional populations on some Caribbean islands. In Costa Rica, it is a localized resident rather than a widespread species, recorded mainly in the lowlands around Golfo Dulce, including areas near Ciudad Neily and south and west toward Panama. It uses overgrown pastures, weedy grasslands, rice and sugarcane fields, secondary growth, scrub, and other open habitats created or maintained by disturbance.
value.migrationStatus: Resident in Costa Rica. It is not known to undertake regular long-distance migration; individuals occupy suitable lowland habitat throughout the year. Its Costa Rican range appears to have expanded northward from Chiriquí, Panama, following forest clearing, although the extent and timing of this expansion remain imperfectly documented.
value.breeding: Crested Bobwhites are ground-nesting birds. The nest is typically a shallow, concealed depression or scrape hidden among grasses or other low vegetation, where camouflage helps protect the eggs and young. Pairs or small groups may breed in open habitats with enough cover for nesting and nearby feeding areas. Detailed information on nesting dates, clutch size, and breeding success in Costa Rica is limited, so local breeding patterns are not well established.
value.dietFeeding: The diet consists mainly of seeds, grains, and other plant material gathered from the ground, supplemented by insects and other small invertebrates. In Costa Rica, it may feed in grasslands, cultivated fields, and field margins, where fallen seeds and arthropods are available. It usually forages by walking and probing among vegetation or leaf litter, and may remain concealed until approached closely before flushing.
value.behavior: Crested Bobwhites are secretive, terrestrial birds that usually move through vegetation in pairs or small coveys. They spend much of their time walking, foraging, and sheltering in dense grass or low scrub. When disturbed, they generally prefer to run or freeze rather than fly, but they can make a rapid, low flight to escape danger. Their social groups are often smaller than those of the Spot-bellied Bobwhite.

conservation.populationTrend: The global population is considered large, and no reliable evidence indicates a rapid overall decline. Detailed population monitoring is limited, particularly in Costa Rica.
